outcome: Nothing since 26 January 2024 has been found that gives explicit necessary and sufficient conditions on periodic curvature and torsion for the curve they determine to be closed. The general (non-explicit) closure criteria date from 1956 (Schmeidler, secondhand) and 1981 (Hwang), and I could not read either in full. The one in-window item on this inverse problem is Bamba and Ogata (DOI 10.1007/s00022-025-00792-3, 2025), which constructs closed space curves from periodic curvature and torsion; I could not read the paper itself. The other in-window papers that touch this area (Honda–Tanaka–Yamauchi 2024; Ghomi–Raffaelli 2024) ask different questions.
problem_asks: The frozen bullet asks for the following, taken part by part. (1) Two periodic functions, with a common period L. The bullet does not name them; MathWorld and the literature I found read them as the curvature kappa(s) and torsion tau(s) of a space curve, parametrised by arclength, and I have adopted that reading. (2) The integral curve determined by those two functions: the space curve with that curvature and torsion, up to rigid motion. (3) Necessary conditions on (kappa, tau) for that curve to be closed. (4) Sufficient conditions on (kappa, tau) for that curve to be closed. (5) Both sets of conditions are to be explicit, per the parenthetical in the statement. (6) 'Closed' is not defined in the bullet. I read it as the curve returning to its starting point with its Frenet frame, possibly after a length other than L, so a criterion has to cover any closing length, not only L. (7) The bullet is not restricted to plane or space curves. The literature treats the planar case (torsion identically zero) and the spatial case separately, and I read the bullet as covering both.

events.what_happened: W. Schmeidler, 'Notwendige und hinreichende Bedingungen dafür, dass eine Raumkurve geschlossen ist' (Archiv der Mathematik (Basel) 7 (1956), 384–385), as described by Giusteri and Fried (arXiv:1611.07155, Section 5). They say it gives a general closure criterion for a space curve with continuous curvature and torsion, stated as a monodromy-type condition: a suitable restriction of the operator U(L;0) equals the identity. I did not open Schmeidler's paper; it was not reachable. The description is secondhand.
events.delivers: According to the secondhand description, a necessary and sufficient condition for closure of a space curve with continuous curvature and torsion, in operator (monodromy) form. Closure of the curve with given periodic kappa and tau is captured only implicitly, through the solution of the Frenet system. No explicit formula in kappa and tau is reported. Giusteri and Fried state that an explicit expression of U(L;0) is available only in very special cases.
events.remains: Explicit conditions on kappa and tau, since the criterion is stated through the solution of the Frenet system. Whether that meets the statement's '(explicit)' is for the judging pass.

checked_by.qualification: Authors of a 2016 paper on Cosserat rods and framed curves that treats the closed-curve problem in detail
checked_by.what_they_did: Restated Schmeidler's general solution as the comparison point for their own closure conditions, describing it as identical in spirit. They did not independently verify Schmeidler's theorem, and I found no other check of it.

events.direction: Gives a general closure criterion for continuous curvature and torsion, in implicit monodromy form. On the secondhand description it answers the question in principle, not in explicit form.

events.what_happened: J. Weiner, Pacific Journal of Mathematics 74 (2), 1978, as summarised in a search result. The summary says it obtains necessary conditions on the length, curvature and torsions of a curve in order that it be closed. The identification of the author and the result comes from that search summary. I did not open the paper.
events.delivers: Necessary conditions on length, curvature and torsion for a curve to be closed, per the search summary. Not sufficient conditions.
events.remains: Sufficiency, and any explicit characterisation of closure for given periodic kappa and tau.
events.direction: Necessary conditions only. Cuts toward the expected answer that periodicity and length constraints are needed, without a closure criterion.

events.what_happened: Cheng Chung Hwang, 'A differential-geometric criterion for a space curve to be closed', Proc. Amer. Math. Soc. 83 (1981), 357–361, DOI 10.1090/S0002-9939-1981-0624931-0. The AMS abstract, as shown in a search listing, says the paper gives a necessary and sufficient condition on the curvature and torsion of a space curve that guarantees the curve is closed (periodic). I could not open the AMS page or PDF; both returned 403. Ari and Önder (arXiv:1003.2040, abstract opened) say this answers a question Shiing-Shen Chern raised in 1978. They say Chung's method uses the Frenet frame and Picard's successive approximation, and that for constant curvature and torsion the curve is periodic iff tau = 0 and kappa = 2 pi / omega. Ari and Önder name the author 'H. C. Chung'. I could not read their restatement of the criterion, since the arXiv PDF returned binary.
events.revisions: No preprint found. I take the 1981 publication as the first public written argument; the month is not established.
events.delivers: A necessary and sufficient condition on kappa and tau for a space curve (in Euclidean R^3) to be closed, per the AMS abstract. Its exact form is not read by me. Per Ari and Önder's summary, it recovers the constant-data case as tau = 0, kappa = 2 pi / omega. The abstract states no separate periodicity hypothesis.
events.remains: Whether the criterion is explicit in kappa and tau, as the statement's parenthetical asks. The abstract does not say whether it is an integral or iterative condition. Nothing else in the bullet is left open by the abstract.

checked_by.qualification: Authors of a 2010 arXiv paper that restates this criterion and generalises it to n-space curves in Minkowski space-time
checked_by.what_they_did: Took the Chung/Hwang criterion as the starting point of their own generalisation. I read only their abstract, not the restated criterion.

events.direction: Cuts toward a complete classical answer for space curves. It claims the necessary and sufficient condition Chern asked for in 1978, which would make the bullet's question answered in general, subject to whether the criterion counts as explicit.
people: Cheng Chung Hwang (credited as H. C. Chung by Ari and Önder)
Shiing-Shen Chern (posed the question in 1978, per Ari and Önder)

events.what_happened: P. Caldiroli and M. Guida, 'Closed curves in R^3 with prescribed curvature and torsion in perturbative cases, Part 1: Necessary condition and study of the unperturbed problem', Rend. Lincei Mat. Appl. 17 (2006), no. 3, 227–242, DOI 10.4171/RLM/466. I read the EMS Press record. They study (kappa, tau)-loops, closed curves in R^3 with prescribed curvature and torsion. They state a necessary condition for a bounded sequence of such loops to exist when kappa_n and tau_n converge to 1 and 0, and prove Fredholm-type properties for the unperturbed problem kappa = 1, tau = 0.
events.revisions: EMS Press gives journal publication on 30 September 2006. A preprint is hosted on the University of Turin IRIS repository, but I did not establish its date.
events.delivers: A necessary condition for the existence of bounded sequences of (kappa, tau)-loops, in the perturbative regime near the constant data kappa = 1, tau = 0. Fredholm properties for the unperturbed case. This is an existence statement for loops with prescribed functions, not a characterisation of when given periodic kappa and tau close up.
events.remains: The whole bullet. The paper gives no closure characterisation for given data, and it is confined to perturbations of the constant case.
events.time_since_posted: about 20 years. A search summary reports Musina (2011, PAMS) citing Part 1 in its bibliography; that is citation, not checking, and I did not verify it.
events.direction: Neither toward nor against a closure criterion. It is an existence result near the constant case.

events.what_happened: P. Caldiroli and M. Guida, 'Closed curves in R^3 with prescribed curvature and torsion in perturbative cases, Part 2: Sufficient conditions', Rend. Lincei Mat. Appl. 17 (2006), no. 4, 291–307, DOI 10.4171/RLM/470. I did not open the paper. From a search summary, branches of (kappa, tau)-loops for small perturbations emanate from circles, corresponding to stable zeros of a vector field M: T^2 x R^3 to R^5.
events.delivers: Existence of branches of closed loops near circles, for small perturbation parameters, per the search summary. Not a characterisation of closure for given periodic kappa and tau.
events.remains: The whole bullet, apart from the perturbative existence near circles.
events.direction: Neither toward nor against a closure criterion. It is a perturbative existence result.

events.what_happened: P. G. Grinevich and M. U. Schmidt, 'Closed curves in R^3: a characterization in terms of curvature and torsion, the Hasimoto map and periodic solutions of the Filament Equation', arXiv:dg-ga/9703020, submitted 26 March 1997 (single version). I opened the arXiv abstract. It says that for a closed curve in R^3 the curvature and torsion are periodic and satisfy extra constraints, which can be stated as a spectral problem for a 2x2 matrix differential operator from the self-focusing NLS. The paper also gives a spectral characterisation of Bloch varieties generating periodic solutions of the Filament Equation, via isoperiodic deformations. The body was not readable to me. A search summary of the paper's content says that, for the curve their Lemma 1 constructs from a nonvanishing complex curvature q(s), period 2 pi closure is equivalent to two conditions, the first being that a 2x2 matrix E-hat_1(s) is 2 pi-periodic. The second condition was not reported.
events.revisions: Single version, v1, 26 Mar 1997 (16 KB), per the arXiv abstract page.
events.delivers: A spectral characterisation of closure for a class of curves built from periodic data (the curves in its Lemma 1, and periodic solutions of the Filament Equation). Closure is reduced to periodicity of a matrix and a second condition. Per the abstract, the constraints on closed curves are stated through a spectral problem, not as an explicit formula in kappa and tau.
events.remains: A criterion for arbitrary periodic kappa and tau, in explicit form. The paper's characterisation is spectral and is restricted to the class its method constructs. The second closure condition was not read.

checked_by.qualification: Authors of a 2018 arXiv pair (1801.07032; 1901.03242) on closed finite-gap curves, which builds on the Grinevich–Schmidt framework
checked_by.what_they_did: Describe the Grinevich–Schmidt deformation as preserving intrinsic and extrinsic periodicity, per a search summary of their body. I did not read that passage directly.

events.direction: Cuts toward an exact closure characterisation, but only for a special class, in spectral form. It neither confirms nor refutes an explicit criterion for general periodic data.

events.what_happened: O. Zubelevich, a 2017 note, as summarised in a search result. It gives sufficient conditions for a curve in R^3 to be unbounded, expressed in terms of its curvature and torsion. I did not open it and did not locate a URL.
events.delivers: Sufficient conditions for unboundedness of a space curve in terms of curvature and torsion, per the search summary. This is not closure.
events.remains: The whole bullet. Unboundedness is a different property from closure.
events.direction: Neither toward nor against closure. A neighbouring property.

events.what_happened: J. Mostovoy and R. Sadykov, 'Approximations of periodic functions to R^n by curvatures of closed curves', arXiv:1205.5892, submitted 26 May 2012. I opened the arXiv abstract. For n periodic real functions with a common period, the first n-1 of them positive, and any tolerance e > 0, there is a closed curve in R^{n+1} whose first n curvatures stay within e of those functions at every point. The abstract adds that the analogous result fails for closed curves in hyperbolic space and for parametric families.
events.revisions: v1 26 May 2012 per the arXiv abstract page. I did not check later versions.
events.delivers: Existence of closed curves in R^{n+1} whose curvatures approximate prescribed periodic functions to any tolerance, with positivity of the first n-1 functions. Approximate and existential. It does not say when given exact periodic functions determine a closed curve.
events.remains: Exact closure criteria. The converse question (given exact kappa and tau, is the curve closed?) is not addressed.
events.time_since_posted: about 14 years. I did not do a citation search for this paper.
events.direction: Cuts toward existence of closed curves with approximately prescribed periodic curvature. It answers the converse question, not the closure criterion asked.

events.what_happened: Z. Ari and M. Önder, 'On Closed Space Curves In Minkowski Space-Time', arXiv:1003.2040, submitted 10 March 2010. I opened the abstract. It generalises the criterion for a 3-space curve to be closed (the Chung/Hwang criterion, cited as [3]) to n-space curves in Minkowski space-time E^n_v, and applies this to curves on oriented surfaces in Minkowski space.
events.revisions: v1 10 Mar 2010 per the arXiv abstract page. I did not check later versions.
events.delivers: A closure criterion for curves in Minkowski space-time, as a generalisation of the Euclidean 3-space criterion. The restriction is to the Lorentzian ambient space.
events.remains: The Euclidean space-curve question the bullet asks about is not changed by this paper.
events.time_since_posted: about 16 years. I found no published verification of this paper.
events.direction: An analogue in a different ambient geometry. It does not change the Euclidean statement.

events.what_happened: S. Klein and M. Kilian, 'On Closed Finite Gap Curves in Spaceforms I', arXiv:1801.07032, first submitted 22 January 2018 (latest revision v5, 4 March 2020). Published in SIGMA 16 (2020), 011. I opened the arXiv abstract. It says closed finite-gap curves are dense, in the W^{2,2} Sobolev norm, among closed curves in R^3 and S^3. The abstract does not discuss closing conditions. A search summary of the body says finite-gap solutions close only under extra closing conditions expressed through the monodromy of an extended frame, depending on the space form. I did not read the body.
events.revisions: v1 22 Jan 2018; v5 4 Mar 2020; journal SIGMA 16 (2020) 011, per the search summary.
events.delivers: Density of closed finite-gap curves among closed curves in R^3 and S^3, in the W^{2,2} norm. Per the abstract, that is all. The closing-conditions statement is from a search summary of the body, not verified.
events.remains: A closure criterion for arbitrary periodic kappa and tau. Density of a special class is a different question.
events.direction: A different question: density of a special class of closed curves. It neither resolves nor refutes the closure criterion.

events.what_happened: G. G. Giusteri and E. Fried, 'Importance and effectiveness of representing the shapes of Cosserat rods and framed curves as paths in the special Euclidean algebra', arXiv:1611.07155, submitted 22 November 2016. I read the arXiv abstract metadata and the Section 5 passages of the ar5iv HTML. They restate the Efimov–Fenchel problem as the question of necessary and sufficient conditions on curvature and torsion for the curve to be closed, and state that closure amounts to a suitable restriction of U(L;0) being the identity map. They say this solution is identical in spirit to Schmeidler's, and later Hwang's, for continuous curvature and torsion fields. A search summary says they extend this to square-integrable curvature and measure-valued torsion; I did not verify that. They note that an explicit expression of U(L;0) is available only in very special cases.
events.revisions: v1 22 Nov 2016 per the arXiv abstract page. Later versions not checked.
events.delivers: A restatement of the general monodromy-form closure criterion, and per the search summary an extension to square-integrable curvature and measure-valued torsion. It establishes no new explicit criterion for kappa and tau, and says explicit forms exist only in special cases.
events.remains: The explicit criterion in kappa and tau, which the paper itself says is available only in special cases.
events.direction: Restates the general implicit criterion and extends it to different hypotheses (square-integrable curvature, measure-valued torsion). A different-hypotheses version, so not a resolution of the explicit question for the bullet.

events.what_happened: H. Karcher, 'Closed Constant Curvature Space Curves', arXiv:2004.10284, submitted 21 April 2020. I opened the abstract. It uses ODEs and symmetry arguments to construct closed constant-curvature space curves, first on cylinders, then on tori, then with the Frenet–Serret equations.
events.revisions: v1 21 Apr 2020 per the arXiv abstract page.
events.delivers: Constructions of closed constant-curvature space curves, using symmetry. A special case with constant kappa. No criterion for periodic kappa and tau in general.
events.remains: The general closure criterion for arbitrary periodic kappa and tau.
events.direction: Constructive, and a special case (constant curvature). It does not change the general question.

events.what_happened: K. Honda, M. Tanaka and K. Yamauchi, 'The total absolute curvature of closed curves with singularities', arXiv:2403.00487, March 2024 (arXiv identifier 2403). I did not open the paper. From a search summary, they extend Fenchel's theorem to closed frontals and show that a non-co-orientable closed frontal in R^n has total absolute curvature at least pi.
events.delivers: A lower bound on total absolute curvature for closed frontals (per the search summary). A total-curvature bound, not a closure criterion.
events.remains: The whole bullet. A total-curvature bound does not decide whether given periodic kappa and tau close up.
events.direction: A different question: a total-curvature bound, for frontals. Discounted for this bullet.

events.what_happened: M. Ghomi and M. Raffaelli, 'h-Principles for curves and knots of constant torsion', arXiv:2410.06027, first posted October 2024; the HTML version was last revised 3 October 2025. Per a search summary, the paper is published in Comment. Math. Helv. (2026), DOI 10.4171/CMH/622. They show that curves of constant torsion satisfy a C^1-dense h-principle, and that there is a knot of constant torsion in each isotopy class. I did not open the paper.
events.revisions: First posted October 2024 (arXiv 2410); HTML revised 3 Oct 2025; journal publication per the search summary.
events.delivers: Existence of constant-torsion curves and knots in each isotopy class, via an h-principle. This does not concern closure of curves with given periodic curvature and torsion.
events.remains: The whole bullet. The paper treats constant torsion, not periodic data.
events.direction: A different question: existence of constant-torsion knots, not closure for periodic data. Discounted for this bullet.

events.what_happened: K. Bamba and Y. Ogata, 'Closed space curves with singularities, generated by periodic curvature and torsion', Journal of Geometry, DOI 10.1007/s00022-025-00792-3. I did not read the paper. Springer's page redirected to a login, and the DOI resolver redirected there too. I know it from an aggregator record (synapsesocial, which says 'No abstract yet') and from a Japanese conference abstract by Bamba, which I read only as a search summary. The talk abstract frames the inverse problem (which periodic curvature, or curvature and torsion, produce a closed curve) as the 'closed curve problem'. It says the problem is almost entirely unexplored, and that the work constructs closed space curves, including with singularities, from periodic kappa and tau. It does not, as far as I could read, state a closure criterion. I found no arXiv preprint.
events.revisions: The aggregator lists the year as 2026 and a publication date of 3 March 2026. The DOI suffix 025 suggests 2025 registration. The first public written argument is not established.
events.delivers: Per the talk abstract only: constructions of closed space curves, including closed curves with singularities, from periodic curvature and torsion. Whether it provides any necessary and sufficient condition, or any sufficient family of periodic data giving closure, is unknown to me.
events.remains: Not established. The abstract I read claims no criterion for general periodic kappa and tau.
events.time_since_posted: between about 7 and 19 months, depending on which date is right
events.direction: Constructive. If its constructions give closure for given periodic data, it is a partial or sufficient-condition result. I cannot classify it from what I read.

disputes.summary: The author of the 1981 criterion is 'Cheng Chung Hwang' on the AMS record, and 'H. C. Chung' in Ari and Önder's text (arXiv:1003.2040). The same paper is clearly meant. I did not resolve the name variant against zbMATH or MathSciNet.

Schmeidler (1956) against Hwang (1981). Giusteri and Fried describe Schmeidler's general solution, 'and later Hwang', as identical in spirit. Ari and Önder, and the AMS abstract, present 1981 as the answer to Chern's 1978 question. Whether the problem was first settled in 1956 or 1981, and whether either criterion is explicit, is not resolved by the sources I could read. Schmeidler's own paper was not reachable.

Bamba and Ogata's publication year: the DOI suffix 025 suggests 2025, but the aggregator lists the year as 2026 and the publication date as 3 March 2026. The first public written argument is not established.

summary: The frozen bullet does not name curvature or torsion. The MathWorld entry 'Closed Curve Problem' (credited to Weisstein; no references; poses the question and gives no answer) does name them, as kappa(s) and tau(s) with period L, and I read the bullet that way. The bullet's footnote target on the Wikipedia page could not be resolved, so I cannot say which source the list relies on. The problem has a long history before the window. Efimov (1947) and Fenchel (1951) posed it, per Giusteri and Fried's quotation of them. Schmeidler (1956) gave a general monodromy-type closure criterion (secondhand; the original was not reachable). Hwang (1981; credited as H. C. Chung in one source) gave a necessary and sufficient condition on kappa and tau, answering a question Chern raised in 1978 (per Ari and Önder). Whether these settle the bullet turns on the word 'explicit', and this is a close call. Both general criteria are stated through the solution of the Frenet system, or through an operator condition. Giusteri and Fried say that an explicit form of the operator is available only in special cases. I could not read Hwang's criterion (AMS returned 403), so I cannot say whether it is explicit in kappa and tau. Since 26 January 2024 I found no event that changes the criterion. Three in-window items sit near it. Honda, Tanaka and Yamauchi (March 2024) bound total absolute curvature of frontals, a different question. Ghomi and Raffaelli (October 2024) treat constant-torsion curves and knots, also a different question. Bamba and Ogata (2025 per the DOI; Journal of Geometry) construct closed space curves with singularities from periodic kappa and tau, and their talk abstract calls the inverse problem almost unexplored. I could not read their paper, so whether it contains a closure criterion or only constructions is unknown. It is the event that most needs reading. Caldiroli and Guida (2006) study the existence of closed curves with prescribed kappa and tau, perturbatively near circles. That is related, but it is not a characterisation. No qualified human verification of Hwang's criterion or of Bamba–Ogata was found. Ari–Önder and Giusteri–Fried engage with the criterion as the basis for their own generalisations, not as checks. On AI: none of the 41 searches linked an AI system to this problem, and the sources I could read name no system. I have set ai.none_found to true on that basis. That finding does not extend to the unread Bamba–Ogata paper. Other AI claims surfaced in the searches and concern other problems: an August 2026 report of Claude, via Alpöge, on a complex structure on S^6 (the Hopf problem; unverified), Alpöge's Jacobian-conjecture counterexample, OpenAI's Astra results, AlphaEvolve (arXiv 2511.02864), ProofCouncil (arXiv 2607.09474) and Meta's Muse Spark papers. None bears on this bullet, so I have not recorded them as events.
competing_reading: Hwang (1981) gave necessary and sufficient conditions for a space curve to be closed, which is what the bullet asks for. On that reading the problem was settled in 1981, and 'explicit' is at most a presentational demand that the 1981 condition meets. Nothing in the window then changes its status. The opposite reading: the 1956 and 1981 criteria are implicit, stated through a monodromy operator or an iterative construction. The bullet asks for explicit conditions in terms of kappa and tau, so the problem remains open. On that reading the Bamba–Ogata constructions, if they yield explicit families of closed data, are partial progress on the open part.
what_would_settle_it: (1) Read Hwang (1981) in full, from the AMS PDF or the MathSciNet review (MR 624931), to see whether the condition is an explicit inequality or integral in kappa and tau. (2) Read Schmeidler (Archiv der Mathematik 7 (1956), 384–385) to compare its form with Hwang's. (3) Read the Bamba–Ogata main theorem and its acknowledgements and contribution statement in the Springer full text, which is needed for the AI check and for deciding whether the paper gives any criterion. (4) Resolve the Wikipedia footnote for this bullet to see which source the list cites. (5) Run citation tracking for Hwang (1981) and Bamba–Ogata in MathSciNet or zbMATH, to find any later verification or any claimed resolution.
